reason: Only the minimum Node.js version rises (engines >=22.0.0); there is no API change and the template already runs Node 22.

Compared five URL-credential forms on 1.10.0 and 1.20.0: plain credentials and the auth option behave the same, percent-encoded or parser-escaped ones (ada%40ex.com, pa^ss) were sent still-encoded by 1.10 so working 1.10 code could not use them, and the only changed case is a raw credential containing a literal valid %XX sequence pasted into the URL, which is malformed URL input.

Set six Content-Type values with res.set() before res.send() on 5.1.0 and 5.3.0: only malformed ones (a bare charset parameter, ";;", an unquoted space, an unterminated quote) differ, throwing a 500 on 5.1 and sending on 5.3, so code that works on 5.1 behaves the same on 5.3 and no stale variant can fail.

Compared Basic-auth headers from 1.10.0 and 1.20.0 for ASCII, Latin-1, Cyrillic/emoji and lone-surrogate credentials on the http and fetch adapters: passwords encode to the same bytes and the http adapter is unchanged; the only difference is a Latin-1 username on the fetch adapter (raw Latin-1 next to a UTF-8 password on 1.10, UTF-8 on 1.20), which only a server decoding usernames as Latin-1 could notice.

Sent requests through a local proxy with NO_PROXY set to CIDR, exact-IP and hostname lists on 1.10.0 and 1.20.0: only CIDR entries differ (ignored on 1.10, so requests went through the proxy; matched on 1.20), so code written for 1.10 could not use them and none plausibly depends on a CIDR entry being ignored.
